cards.text: Elisha the prophet calls over one of the sons of the prophets and hands him a job. Tuck your cloak under your belt, take this flask of oil, and go to Ramoth-gilead. That's the whole briefing, friend: a flask and a city name, which is barely more instructions than I got in all my years in the junk drawer.

cards.question: Elisha tells the young man who to look for once he gets to Ramoth-gilead. Who is it?

cards.text: Elisha says to go in and get Jehu away from his companions. Whatever this is, friend, it is NOT a group announcement.

cards.question: Once the young prophet gets Jehu away from his companions, where does Elisha tell him to take Jehu?

cards.text: Then the flask comes out: Elisha says pour the oil right on Jehu's head and speak the LORD's words. Walk up to an army commander and pour oil on his HEAD? Friend, that takes more nerve than I've got in my whole mustache.

cards.question: With the oil on Jehu's head, the young prophet is to declare: "This is what the LORD says: I anoint you ___ over Israel."
After he anoints Jehu, Elisha tells the young prophet to stay and wait for Jehu's answer.

cards.text: So the young prophet heads to Ramoth-gilead and walks in on the army commanders, all sitting there together. He says he has a message for the commander, which is like walking into a room FULL of managers and asking to speak to the manager.

cards.question: When the young prophet says he has a message for the commander, Jehu asks which of them it's for.

cards.text: "For you, commander," comes the answer, so Jehu follows him into the house, and the oil goes on his head with the LORD's word: "I anoint you king over the LORD’s people Israel." Friend, Jehu didn't apply, didn't interview, didn't even get a heads-up, and he just got the BIGGEST promotion in the country.

cards.question: The LORD gives Jehu his first job as king: strike down the house of his master. Whose house is it?
What reason does the LORD give Jehu for striking down Ahab's house?

answers.text: To avenge the blood of His prophets
To win back the land from Aram
To give Israel a stronger army

cards.text: Ahab was king of Israel (1 Kings 16:29), Jezebel was his wife (1 Kings 16:31), and the LORD says that blood was shed by Jezebel's hand. Now the whole house of Ahab will perish, made like the houses of Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah.

cards.question: The LORD says someone will give Jezebel a proper burial.

cards.text: On the plot of ground at Jezreel the dogs will devour her, and there will be no one to bury her. Then the young prophet opens the door and RUNS, just like Elisha said, and I respect a man who follows instructions all the way out the door.

cards.question: Jehu walks back out to his master's servants, and they ask him: "Is everything all right? Why did this ___ come to you?"

cards.text: Jehu brushes it off, like it's just prophet babble, and they fire right back: "That is a lie!" and "Tell us now!" I bet they saw that man SPRINT out of the house, friend, so Jehu tells them the LORD's words: he's been anointed king over Israel.

cards.question: Quickly, each man takes his ___ and puts it under Jehu on the bare steps.
Right there on the steps, the men blow the ram's horn and proclaim Jehu king.

cards.text: One minute Jehu's sitting in a meeting, the next he's got a crown and a pile of garments under his feet. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "This is what the LORD says: I anoint you ___ over Israel.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 16 quotes "Is everything all right? Why did this ___ come to you?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: "That's the whole briefing, friend: a flask and a city name" says the text gives no more instructions. Elisha goes on in 2 Kings 9:2-3 to tell the young prophet who to find, where to take him, what to pour, what to say, and to run. The line states something the text shows is untrue.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke "that takes more nerve than I've got in my whole mustache" does not land right away. A mustache is not something that holds or measures nerve, so the image needs explaining. It also leans on the mustache, which papa-dorin.md says is not his main source of jokes.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: In "After he anoints Jehu, Elisha tells the young prophet..." the pronoun "he" comes before anyone is named. It reads as if Elisha does the anointing. The question should name the young prophet as the one who anoints.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This story card carries more than two beats. It has the prophet's reply "For you, commander," Jehu going into the house, the oil and the LORD's word, and then the joke. It should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: "The LORD gives Jehu his first job as king" adds an order ("first") that the text does not give. 2 Kings 9:7 only says "you are to strike down the house of your master Ahab."

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Jeroboam son of Nebat and Baasha son of Ahijah show up here for the first time, and the card never says who they are. It also never says what happened to their houses, so "made like the houses of" will mean nothing to the baker.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card carries more than two beats. It introduces Ahab, introduces Jezebel, says the blood was shed by Jezebel's hand, says the whole house of Ahab will perish, and makes the comparison to Jeroboam and Baasha. It should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the servants' exact word ("madman" against "stranger" or "beggar"). That is wording they haven't seen, not meaning they can reason out. "Stranger" could also be argued as true, since nothing in the text shows the commanders knew the young prophet.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "I bet they saw that man SPRINT out of the house" gives a reason why the servants call Jehu's answer a lie. The text gives no reason. Marking it "I bet" is allowed for feelings, not for reasons. The text also says the young prophet ran, not that the servants saw him run.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This story card carries more than two beats. Jehu brushes it off, the servants push back, the joke follows, and then Jehu tells them about the anointing. It should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: "the next he's got a crown" adds a detail that isn't in the text. In 2 Kings 9:13 the men put their garments under Jehu, blow the ram's horn and proclaim him king. No crown is mentioned.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
